intent: Cover unity_handler.sh to a measured 100% and take it OFF the shell-coverage allowlist -- the first entry removed this session, 105 -> 104. Fix the bash hash-cache bug found doing it, which had silently weakened the two suites committed just before.
scope: .../tests/transcribe_harness.sh: new _t_unstub helper; basename added to the restricted PATH
Non-goal: no change to any subject; no latent bug surfaced in unity_handler.sh
changes: HARNESS BUG, found by an assertion that would not go green: bash caches executable locations in a hash table, so `command -v foo` keeps SUCCEEDING after foo is deleted from the stub dir. Every 'tool is missing' test therefore ran as a 'tool is present' test -- asserting the opposite of its own name while looking plausible. Reproduced minimally: after `rm`, STILL FOUND; after `hash -r`, gone.

The fix is a _t_unstub helper that removes the stub and clears the table, applied to all three suites in the directory. The two committed an hour earlier were affected and are corrected here; test_transcribe_pkgmgr.sh goes 15 -> 18 passing assertions as a result, so three of its checks had been vacuous.

`basename` was added to the restricted PATH because the SUBJECT calls it, unlike bash/env which the stubs' shebangs need. The suite avoids needing `tail` by taking the last line with a parameter expansion instead: every binary in that PATH is another thing a shebang can trip over.
The generated .desktop file is asserted on its CONTENT (Exec and MimeType lines), and xdg-mime registration on the BASENAME it is given -- a full path there would silently fail to register.

verification.evidence: unity_handler.sh: 32/32 lines = 100.00%, exit 0 at --min 100. Measured through run_all.sh, the subject is_covered() builds.

verification.command: bash meta/scripts/check_shell_coverage.sh .../unity_handler.sh (AFTER removing it from the allowlist)
verification.evidence: 'every checked shell library meets the coverage bar', exit 0. The lib passes the REAL gate with no exemption -- properly cleared, not merely measured.
15 + 18 + 18 = 51 assertions, 0 failures, 'All transcribe lib test files passed.'

verification.command: minimal repro of the hash cache: stub a command, run it, rm it, then command -v
verification.evidence: 'STILL FOUND (hash cache)' before `hash -r`, 'gone after hash -r'. This is what makes _t_unstub necessary rather than cosmetic.

verification.command: re-measure the other two libs after the harness change
verification.evidence: transcribe_deps.sh 48/52 = 92.31% and transcribe_pkgmgr.sh 49/50 = 98.00%, both unchanged. Both stay on the allowlist.

risks: Any other suite in the repo that removes a stub with a bare `rm` has the same latent defect: its 'missing tool' branch is not being tested. The features/lib suites use a jail and mostly add rather than remove stubs, but this is worth a sweep before the gate is armed.
The restricted PATH must list every binary the subjects use. A missing one surfaces as 'command not found' mid-suite rather than as a clear assertion failure.
rollback: git revert the commit; unity_handler.sh returns to the allowlist and the three suites return to bare `rm` unstubbing.
After rollback, confirm the allowlist is back to 105 entries so the gate's view is unchanged.
